A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FANformer work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original FANformer pretraining, scaling, ablation, arithmetic-generalization and supervised-fine-tuning results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds ULogic logical-reasoning results and a representational-capacity comparison.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same modified FAN projection, cosine/sine and linear feature concatenation, QKV attention, and pre-norm SwiGLU architecture. Equation edits, expanded explanations and the renamed activation variant do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds ULogic stress tests involving multi-premise inferential rules and negated conclusions at Length 3 and Length 4. This is a targeted extension of reasoning coverage; the Dolma data, validation suites, commonsense and instruction-tuning benchmarks, and arithmetic tasks are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds GPT-4 as a scored comparator in the ULogic experiment and MLP in the capacity comparison. Existing language-model and ablation comparator memberships remain unchanged. StableLM's shortened name and FANformer + Activation becoming FANformer (original FAN) do not represent new baselines.

E3.justification: The added studies introduce two-shot chain-of-thought prompting, paired original/negated-rule accuracy, and Lipschitz comparisons across layer depths. Retained training, SFT and Leave-Square-Out protocols remain unchanged. Table 1 revises Llama-3.2-1B's reported size from 1.2B to 1.1B without changing its scores or establishing a different checkpoint.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the analysis with logical-consistency failures illustrated in Figure 13, representational capacity versus depth in Figure 6, and computational overhead under matched-parameter and matched-dimension conditions in Appendix E. The original ablation, hyperparameter-sensitivity and arithmetic-generalization analyses are retained, including relocated material.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, across-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both already specify ten generations per arithmetic test point; this sampling practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The retained main, SFT and detailed ablation tables preserve their performance scores. New Table 3 reports ULogic accuracy of 38.2% for FANformer-1B, 0.0% for OLMo-1B, 7.1% for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 65.1% for GPT-4. Figure 6 adds Lipschitz-versus-depth findings, including a reported 27.3% advantage over Transformer in deeper configurations. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds a group-action definition of periodicity in Section 2 and an elementary FLOP-overhead derivation with a 6.25% upper bound in Appendix E. The ATF equivalence already derived in v1 Appendix F is restated as Proposition 1 with expanded proof presentation in v2 Appendix I.

C1.justification: The core architecture, scaling-efficiency and FANformer-1B contribution claims remain. V2 adds greater representational capacity to its main findings and extends the reasoning claim to ULogic comparisons with OLMo-1B and Qwen2.5-1.5B. Rule learning was already claimed in v1, although v2 also emphasizes it in the abstract.

C2.justification: New Section 2 connects periodicity to reusable inference rules through transformation invariance and a digit-wise addition example. V2 also proposes semantic reuse as an explanation for training dynamics and interprets larger Lipschitz constants and ULogic outcomes as architectural advantages. The original limitations, including uncertainty about the underlying mechanism, remain in Appendix K.

D1.justification: The reported hardware changes from eight Tesla A100-PCIe-40G GPUs to 80 A100 GPUs, and reported pretraining cost changes from approximately 4,700 to 47,600 GPU hours. Appendix J.5 adds ULogic rule-pool, prompting and scoring details. These materially revise resource and reproducibility information without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references concerning ULogic, group actions, Lipschitz capacity, non-contradiction, contamination and chain-of-thought prompting, and removes the GELU reference. Its central positioning relative to FAN, FNet and attention-mechanism variants remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Motivation replaces preliminary material moved to Appendix B; the hyperparameter discussion and limitations move to appendices; related work is condensed; and the equivalence derivation becomes a proposition-and-proof presentation. The abstract, introduction, conclusion and variant terminology are also edited.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. V2 adds ULogic Table 3, capacity Figure 6, computational-cost Table 5 and case-study Figure 13. Existing hyperparameter and training/test-accuracy figures are relocated rather than removed.

improvement.justification: V2 gives the rule-learning claim an additional direct test beyond v1's arithmetic experiments, with documented ULogic prompting, scoring and an illustrative case, while preserving the original empirical evidence. The gain is limited: the Lipschitz study lacks estimation details, and Equation (11) incorrectly drops an output-cost term in an equality, although its final upper bound survives. The additions strengthen support without resolving the mechanism limitations.
